articles.titleOriginal: Diving into the details: a chat with perfectionist Chen Yuxi
articles.titleJa: ディテールを掘り下げる：完璧主義者の陳玉熙とのチャット
articles.summaryJa: 2026年の愛知・名古屋アジア競技大会で2つの金メダルを獲得した中国のダイビングスター、チェン・ユーシーは表彰台の向こうに目を向け続けています。China Dailyのオンライン番組Spotlightとの独占的な会話で、Chenはアジア競技大会の旅、各ダイビングの背後にある考え方、そして常に改善を追求していることを振り返ります。
articles.summaryOriginal: Winning two gold medals at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, Chinese diving star Chen Yuxi continues to look beyond the podium. In an exclusive conversation with China Daily's online show Spotlight , Chen reflects on her Asian Games journey, the mindset behind each dive, and her constant pursuit of improvement. For Chen, diving is like polishing a piece of artwork — there is always something to refine, and every competition brings new experiences and challenges. More than a sport, diving has also become an inseparable part of her life. To find out more, click the video.

articles.titleOriginal: Trump says S. Korea deal 'keeps getting better,' unveils $8.4 bil. oil recovery project
articles.titleJa: トランプ大統領、韓国との取引は「良くなり続けている」と述べ、84億$の石油回収プロジェクトを発表
articles.summaryJa: 米国のドナルド・トランプ大統領は金曜日、ワシントンで韓国との合意が改善し続けていると述べ、84億$の石油回収強化プロジェクトを発表した。彼の発言は、ソウルとワシントンが昨年の貿易協定に基づく韓国の投資コミットメントを実施するために取り組んでいるときに行われた。
articles.summaryOriginal: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday in Washington that the South Korea deal keeps getting better, announcing an $8.4 billion enhanced oil recovery project. His remarks came as Seoul and Washington work to implement South Korea’s investment commitment under last year’s trade deal. Trump said the project would support American energy dominance and security, but he gave no details. Seoul said the oil recovery project is not among the strategic investments it agreed to. President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office of the White House, Wednesday, in Washington. AP-Yonhap

articles.summaryOriginal: Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Hana Bank reported data breaches in Seoul on Friday, heightening concerns in the financial sector over AI-powered cyberattacks. KB Kookmin said 119 customers were affected, while Hana Bank said 89 customers had their personal information exposed. Regulators held an emergency response meeting and dispatched investigators to the affected firms. From left are headquarters of KB Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank in Seoul / Korea Times file
